Apple Watch Series 12 is a major upgrade to the core health and fitness tracking wearable, thanks to a brand new health sensing system that includes more powerful heart rate monitoring capabilities.

The new hardware brings more than just more accurate health data. In Apple's promotional materials, I noticed a small but complex feature has undergone a significant change. This is just one of the things I'm excited about with the new Series 12 and Ultra 4.

Apple's heart rate complication feature gets an upgrade on the Series 12 and Ultra 4 models

I love glancing at my Apple Watch and seeing recent heart rate data. A low resting heart rate is a good indicator that I'm doing the right things with my fitness (and stress management).

Therefore, I frequently use Apple's heart rate complication feature on my watch face.

The small circular version is just a launcher, showing the heart rate app icon. The wide version shows recent heart rate readings, along with a heart rate graph from midnight to now.

I use the wide version because it actually shows information. The app launcher version isn't very useful to me.

However, based on the promotional materials for the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4, the smaller heart rate complication feature appears to have received a major upgrade.

For the first time, Apple is showing it displaying actual heart rate numbers, meaning it can serve as a smaller complication component, not just limited to the three-row wide version.

The same complication feature on the Apple Watch Series 11 and Ultra 3 running the watchOS 27 candidate version is still just an app launcher.

The reason is most likely that the new health sensing system reads heart rate every five seconds, a 60-fold improvement over previous Apple Watch versions.

This means the complication can display real-time readings. The wide version requires space to provide before-and-after comparisons of heart rate reading timestamps.

These subtle changes accumulate to make the overall product better, benefiting all users.

Apple Watch Series 12 is available for pre-order starting today, priced from $399. Apple Watch Ultra 4 is also available for pre-order, priced from $799. Both models will officially go on sale a week later on September 18.
